source: NYISO real-time zonal LBMP & Moses South interface flow, Jan 2023 – Dec 2025
findings: K · Long Island had the highest average price at $41.38/MWh, followed by F · Capital ($34.84/MWh) and J · New York City ($33.71/MWh).
K · Long Island's average price was $18.15/MWh above the cheapest zone, D · North ($23.23/MWh).
K · Long Island had the heaviest congestion: on average it added $14.33/MWh to the price, ahead of F · Capital ($8.73/MWh) and J · New York City ($6.97/MWh).
Congestion lowered the average price in A · West (by $0.10/MWh) and D · North (by $1.61/MWh), consistent with power being trapped on the generating side of transmission limits.
All 3 highest-price zones are also among the 3 most congested: K · Long Island, F · Capital and J · New York City.
Across all zone-months, heavier congestion tends to come with higher prices: a strong correlation (r = -0.73).
The link is strongest in NYC & Long Island (J–K) (r = -0.79) and weakest in Upstate (A–E) (r = -0.13).
The most extreme single 5-minute congestion value was -$2,928.14/MWh in F · Capital (Feb 2023), far beyond its monthly average.
cannot_conclude: Higher congestion in a zone does not tell us which transmission line was the bottleneck.
Congestion and price moving together does not prove congestion caused the higher price; weather, fuel prices and demand affect both.
Average $/MWh cannot be turned into total dollars paid, because zone electricity usage is not in this data.
